systemPrompt.append: Workers. This session can start workers with the mcp_sigma_start_worker tool. A worker is an agent in a conversation of its own, which the user can open, watch and talk to. Every worker you start, on your provider too, starts from your message alone, with none of your history, so write a complete brief. Start a worker when the user asks for one, or names a model or a provider for part of the work. Pass the provider and model they named, unchanged, in `provider` and `model`. When they name several, start one worker for each. With none named, leave `provider` out and the worker runs on your own models. For a quick helper inside your own turn, use your own subagent tool if you have one, or do the work yourself.

tools.name: start_worker
tools.description:
Starts a worker: an agent in a conversation of its own, which the user can open, watch and talk to, and which keeps working after your turn ends. Returns the worker's task name at once. Its final answer comes back through wait_worker, or as a message when you are not waiting.
If your task is `/root/task1` and you name a worker "scout", its task name is `/root/task1/scout`. You can call it `scout` or `/root/task1/scout`; other agents reach it by its full name.
A worker runs on your provider and model unless you name others. Set `provider` and `model` only to what the user named, unchanged. The providers are script (a scripted model), claude (Claude Code), openai (ChatGPT), agy (Antigravity's agy). On your provider the worker has your tools. A worker starts from your message alone, with none of your history or instructions, so write a complete brief, when it runs on another provider or you run in a harness (Claude Code or agy); otherwise it starts with your history, unless `fork_turns` is "none". On another provider it runs that provider's default model when you name none.
Start workers only when the user, or instructions such as AGENTS.md or a skill, ask for workers, delegation or parallel work.

task_name.description: Name for the worker. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

message.description: The worker's task, in plain text.

provider.description: The provider to run the worker on, exactly as the user named it: script, claude, openai, agy. Omit to use yours.

model.description: The model to run the worker on, exactly as the user named it. Omit to use yours, or the provider's default on another provider.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for the worker. Omit to use yours.

agent_type.description: Agent type for the worker, one your instructions list under Agent types. Omit unless explicitly asked.

fork_turns.description: Your history to give the worker: "all", the default on your provider, or "none". A worker on another provider, or one you start from a harness (Claude Code or agy), always starts with none.

tools.name: message_worker
tools.description: Sends a message to a worker, or to any agent of your tree by its task name. A working one reads it at its next step; an idle one reads it with its next task. Starts no new turn.

target.description: The worker's task name, as start_worker returned it, or relative to yours.

tools.name: assign_worker
tools.description: Gives a worker a follow-up task, and starts it working if it is idle. A working worker takes the task at its next step. Its answer comes back through wait_worker.

target.description: The worker's task name, as start_worker returned it, or relative to yours.

tools.name: wait_worker
tools.description: Waits for your workers and returns what they sent: a finished worker's final answer, or a message from one. What it returns is not delivered to you again. Returns timed_out true when nothing arrives in time; call it again to keep waiting. Returns early, with nothing received, when the user sends new input.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: list_workers
tools.description: Lists the agents of your tree, you and the workers under you, each by task name with whether it is running, done, interrupted or failed. Optionally filtered by task-name prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-name prefix, without a trailing slash. Omit to list them all.

tools.name: stop_worker
tools.description: Stops a worker's current turn, if any, and returns its previous status. The worker stays available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: The worker's task name, as start_worker returned it, or relative to yours.

availableCommands.name: run-workflow
availableCommands.description: How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

availableCommands.name: swarm
availableCommands.description: (Preview & Quota Heavy) Run a swarm: several agents working in parallel on one task, each in its own conversation, collaborating through a shared message board. Use when the work splits into pieces that can be done at the same time, or when a second pair of eyes should check the first pair's work.
